companyDescription: Social AI Megacap · 3.2B daily users · Meta Glasses $299 launched Jun 23 · Muse Spark closed AI model · $125–145B capex cycle
priceNote: Down 24% from $796 52-wk high — only $42 above 52-wk low; Q2 earnings Jul 29 = 28-day catalyst
summary: Meta trades 24% below its $796 52-week high — a rare discount for a company still growing revenue +33% YoY with 3.2B daily users and an emerging AI hardware story (Meta Glasses launched June 23 at $299). Q2 earnings on July 29 is the pivotal event: 40 analysts average $829 price target implies +47% upside if capex commentary doesn't spook the market again.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Revenue guide $58–61B. The single biggest catalyst: market will focus on capex ROI signals and whether Zuckerberg reins in or expands the $125–145B spend. Any capex reduction = significant re-rate higher.

catalysts.name: Meta Glasses ($299) — Commercial Launch
catalysts.description: Own-brand Meta AI glasses launched Jun 23 at $299 (Adventurer/Fury models). Bundled with Muse Spark AI. Q1 IDC data: META holds 69.2% of AI glasses market. Q2 sell-through data = next read.

catalysts.name: Muse Spark — Closed AI Model Adoption
catalysts.description: Meta pivoted from open Llama to closed Muse Spark (Meta Superintelligence Labs). Claims 10x compute efficiency vs Llama 4. Enterprise + developer adoption metrics at Q2 call.

catalysts.name: EU DSA Child Safety Ruling
catalysts.description: Preliminary breach finding April 29; fine ceiling $12B. Final ruling expected July–Sep 2026. Settlement/smaller fine = relief rally; max fine = negative overhang resolved either way.

risks: AI capex blowout — $125–145B 2026 spend; investors punished the Q1 beat with -8.55% on capex guide. FCF yield shrinks at 20x PE.
EU DSA child safety fine up to $12B — final ruling pending July–September 2026
EU antitrust — WhatsApp AI blocking rival tools; DMA violation possible
Technically weak — stock $42 above 52-wk low of $520; any Q2 miss breaks that support
Closed AI pivot risk — abandoning open-source Llama risks developer ecosystem backlash
AI glasses competition — Google + Samsung Android XR glasses arriving Fall 2026 threatens 69% market share
Capex ROI timeline — $145B annual spend; market questions monetization before 2027

estimateDates.note: Revenue guide $58–61B; capex commentary is the single biggest catalyst. Any trim = relief rally.
Final ruling on child safety breach; max fine $12B. Settlement = overhang removed.

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed at 3.50–3.75%; Warsh removed easing bias Jun 17. META's 20x PE is cheap for a mega-cap — more rate-resilient than high-multiple peers.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core PCE 3.4% (3-yr high). Digital advertising is partially resilient to inflation — brands shift online spend when costs rise. Iran conflict = energy inflation but minimal direct impact.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Digital advertising holds in mild recession. The real risk is enterprise AI capex ROI uncertainty slowing the narrative, not macro directly.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — 20x PE provides some macro cushion vs. high-multiple AI plays. Key risk is capex overreach optics rather than direct macro damage.

catalystSpot.preRunup: Mega-cap social platforms historically run 5–10% in the week before earnings when near 52-wk lows. Positioning is washed out — any positive pre-earnings catalyst (early sell-through data for glasses, analyst upgrades) can accelerate the move.

postWin.note: META historically moves ±11.8% on earnings (median ±11%). Q4 2024 produced +10%. Sustainable upside requires capex steady or reduced + ad revenue acceleration.

postLose.note: Q1 2026 beat -8.55% on capex shock. If Q2 capex raised to $150B+ or revenue misses low-end $58B, tests 52-wk low $520.

spotSizing.reason: Rare mega-cap at 20x PE with +47% consensus upside, near 52-wk low. Core holding sizing — add pre-earnings on any dip to $530–545.
